title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. X is a connected smooth curve over C with smooth compactification X̂ of genus g. D is the reduced boundary divisor, with ν = card(X̂−X) points. Projective connections on X that are regular at infinity (at most simple poles in the sense of the previous page) form a torsor under H^0(X̂, λ(D)), where λ = ω^{⊗2}. Applying ⊗λ to 0→O→O(D)→O(D)/O→0 and using residue-type identifications gives

0→H^0(λ)→H^0(λ(D))→H^0(D, ω|D)→H^1(λ)→H^1(λ(D)).

Previous page, case (a), g≥2: H^1(λ)=0. This gives 0→Ω^1_{M_g}(ξ)→Ω^1_{M_{g,ν}}(ξ)→⊕_{p∈D} ω_p→0, i.e. the cotangent sequence for forgetting the punctures.

This page, case (b), g≤1.
- One asks whether H^1(λ)→H^1(λ(D)) is injective.
- By Serre duality this map is dual to the restriction H^0(X̂, T(-D)) → H^0(X̂, T), where T = ω^{-1} = t_{X̂/C}.
- This is the inclusion Lie Aut(X̂, D) ⊂ Lie Aut(X̂): vector fields vanishing on D inside all vector fields.
- It is injective, so the question becomes surjectivity. Grothendieck calls its cokernel Q(X) = H^0(T)/H^0(T(-D)).
- Dually one gets the four-term exact sequence 0→H^0(ω^2)→H^0(ω^2(D))→H^0(D, ω|D)→Q̌(X)→0. So Q̌(X) measures the failure of the 'cotangent of moduli' sequence to be right exact.

g=1:
- H^0(T) = C (translations). If D≠0, deg T(-D) < 0, so H^0(T(-D)) = 0.
- Hence Q(X) = t_{X̂} and Q̌(X) = ω_{X̂}, the invariant differentials (one-dimensional).
- Therefore dim H^0(ω^2(D)) = 1 + ν − 1 = ν = dim M_{1,ν}.
- He proposes a modular interpretation that absorbs the translation ambiguity. One rigidifies by elliptic curves with origin, ν distinct points, and a chosen point o with νo = Σ p_i. This is a finite-cover rigidification killing infinitesimal translations, hence the remark 'H^0(t)=0'.

g=0:
- H^0(T) = sl_2 has dimension 3.
- H^0(T(-D)) has dimension 2, 1, 0 for ν = 1, 2, ≥3, so Q(X) has dimension 1, 2, 3.
- Hence for ν ≤ 3, dim Q̌ = deg D = dim H^0(D, ω|D). Since H^0(ω^2) = 0, this forces H^0(ω^2(D)) = 0.
- The next page concludes there is a unique regular projective connection when ν ≤ 3. For ν ≥ 4 the space has dimension ν−3 = dim M_{0,ν}, conjecturally ≅ Ω^1_{M_{0,ν}}.

Purpose: to show that the space of regular-singular projective connections (sl_2-opers) on a punctured curve is a torsor under the cotangent space of the moduli space M_{g,ν}. Special care is needed in low genus, where infinitesimal automorphisms obstruct exactness. This feeds the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs theme of the dossier: the uniformizing differential equation as a canonical section.
errors: The general statement 'for 0≤ν≤3, dim Q̌(X) = deg D' is only for g=0. The ν=0 case is trivially consistent: Q = 0 since H^0(T(-D)) = H^0(T).

The remark 'Alors H^0(X̂, t)=0' in the elliptic interpretation is loosely stated. Literally H^0(X̂, t_{X̂}) ≠ 0 for g=1. What is meant is that the rigidified moduli problem has no infinitesimal automorphisms (H^0(T(-D)) = 0 together with the translations being killed). No real gap.

The 'interpretation plausible' via νo = Σ p_i is only sketched. Such o form a torsor under E[ν], so this is a finite étale rigidification, not a change of the dimension count; the cokernel Q̌ = ω_{X̂} is not actually explained by it on the page.

ideas.what: Space of regular-singular projective connections on a punctured curve is an affine space under H^0(X̂, ω^2(D)), identified with the cotangent space of M_{g,ν}
ideas.modern_name: sl_2-opers with regular singularities / projective structures as affine bundle over T*M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, Klein; accessory parameters). Gunning (1967), Hubbard (1981), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche discussions of Teichmüller tower; not explicitly

ideas.what: Serre-duality identification of the obstruction to right-exactness with the dual of Lie Aut(X̂)/Lie Aut(X̂,D)
ideas.modern_name: Deformation theory of pointed curves; H^1(T(-D)) as tangent of M_{g,n}, H^0(T(-D)) as infinitesimal automorphisms

ideas.what: Rigidification of M_{1,ν} by choosing an origin o with νo = sum of the marked points
ideas.modern_name: Level-type rigidification / balanced marking of elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unclear; related to standard rigidifications of M_{1,n}

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the regular projective connection on P^1 minus ≤3 points, and dimension ν−3 for ν≥4
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of hypergeometric equation; accessory parameters for Fuchsian equations on P^1

missed.claim: Elliptic-case rigidification idea: replace the moduli problem of (E, ν points) by (E, origin o, ν points with νo = Σp_i) to kill the translation part of Q(X). This is only a sketched heuristic and is minor.
missed.quote: courbes elliptiques ... à origine et ν pts distincts et un pt choisi o tel que νo soit la somme des dits
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It is a variant of known rigidifications of M_{1,n} and of little novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine but clean Serre-duality computation of low-genus corrections in the identification of regular projective connections with cotangent vectors of M_{g,ν}. The content is classical (Gunning/Hubbard, deformation theory). Its interest is mainly historical, showing Grothendieck around 1972 framing projective structures as a torsor under Ω^1 of moduli stacks.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the sequence: the middle term looks like 'H^0(X, ω^2)^{reg}' (as on the previous/next pages) rather than 'H^0(X̂, ω^2(D))'; the two are the same object.
The third term reads 'H^0(D, ω|D)' (consistent with the previous page) rather than 'H^0(D, ω(D))'.
'Si sinon conoyau dans plus Q(X)' is better read as 'Si non, conoyau dans plus [noté] Q(X)'.
The circled annotations read 'Lie Aut(X̂)' under H^0(X̂, ω^{-1}) and 'Lie Aut(X)' under H^0(X̂, ω^{-1}(-D)).
'(formes diff. inv. sur Jacobienne)' is more plausibly '(formes diff. inv. sur X̂)'. Uncertain.
